mainTopic: Whether the goring-ox משנה follows רבי ישמעאל or רבי עקיבא, then which סלע is the fine for slapping and how the court acquires for the poor
overview: The amud opens in the middle of the discussion about an ox that gores several oxen one after another. The question is whether the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who says the victims are only creditors, or רבי עקיבא, who says each victim becomes a partner in the goring ox. רבא says the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, in a case where each victim seized the ox and became a paid guard over it. רבינא rereads the משנה's words to fit that view, and רבי יוחנן's teaching about negligent guardians supports it. The גמרא then shows that רבי שמעון's money split at the end of the משנה fits רבי עקיבא's partnership view. It accepts that the משנה is split between the two opinions, with support from שמואל and רבי יוחנן. Next comes a new topic: is the סלע fine for slapping someone the valuable צורי coin or the cheap מדינה coin? After a proof is offered and rejected, רב's rule settles it: money set by the רבנן is מדינה money, so the fine is half a זוז. The slapped man gives the money to the poor and then asks for it back. רב יוסף rules that the poor already acquired it, because the court is the 'hand of the poor.' His supporting source about orphans continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the victims are partners, leftover value should go to all of them
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a challenge: according to רבי עקיבא, the משנה should have said the extra value goes back to all the earlier victims, not just the one right before.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'he shall return the extra to the previous victim'?! It should have said 'to all of them'!
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a challenge that started just before this section. The גמרא is attacking the idea that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, each victim becomes a co-owner of the goring ox. If so, any leftover value belongs to all the earlier victims together, so the משנה should say 'return it to all of them.' Since the משנה only mentions the one right before, it seems not to follow רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall return
To the one before him (the previous victim)
To all of them
It should have said

steps.confusionAlert: This section begins in the middle of a sentence. The challenge started earlier on the דף. The words in quotation marks are from the משנה, and the target here is the view of רבי עקיבא that the victims are partners.

phrases.english: "He shall return it to the previous one"?!
It should have said "to all of them"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge against reading the משנה as רבי עקיבא, which began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה as following רבי עקיבא (the victims are partners).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all the earlier victims co-own the ox, the leftover value belongs to all of them. The משנה's wording 'to the previous one' does not fit that.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, because each victim seized the ox and became a paid guard
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה really follows רבי ישמעאל. He answers the earlier challenge ('it should say the first one gains') by setting the case where each victim seized the ox and so became responsible for the damage it does next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל, who says the victims are creditors. You asked why it says 'the last one gains' when it should say 'the first one gains.' Here we are dealing with a case where the victim seized the ox to collect from it, so he became like a paid guard over it, responsible for the damage it does.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי עקיבא's view ran into trouble, רבא goes back to רבי ישמעאל. He repeats the earlier challenge against רבי ישמעאל and answers it by describing a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a creditor, the normal rule would be that the earliest creditor gets paid first. רבא says that here the earlier victim grabbed the ox to collect his payment. That makes him a paid guard (שומר שכר) who is responsible for whatever damage the ox does while he holds it. So when the ox gores again, the next victim collects from the earlier victim's claim, and that is why 'the last one gains.'

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (going back to an earlier position)
Creditors
Each later victim gains
Here, what case are we dealing with? (narrowing the case)
He seized it
A paid guard, who is responsible for losses

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that grabbing an object to collect a debt can turn the creditor into a שומר who is responsible for it.

phrases.english: Rava said: Really, it follows Rabbi Yishmael,
who says they are creditors;
phrases.notes: 'They' means the earlier victims of the goring ox.

phrases.english: and as for what bothered you: "the latest one gains"?!
It should have said "the earliest one gains"!
With what case are we dealing here?
Where the injured party seized it to collect from it,
and he became like a paid bailee over it regarding damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge to רבי עקיבא in step 1, רבא returns to רבי ישמעאל and answers the earlier objection against him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: As creditors, the earliest victim should be paid first, so the משנה should say 'the first one gains.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Each victim seized the ox and became a paid guard over it, so he is responsible for its next goring. That is why the later victim gains.

steps.title: If so, the leftover should go back to the owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: under רבי ישמעאל, the leftover value should go back to the ox's owner, not to the previous victim.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה say 'if there is extra, he returns it to the previous one'? It should have said 'he returns it to the owner'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבא's answer, using a different line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, the owner still owns his ox, and the victims are only creditors. So any value left over after the victims are paid should go back to the owner. The משנה's words 'to the previous one' seem not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Extra, leftover value
To the owner

phrases.english: If so,
"If there is extra in it, he returns it to the previous one"?!
It should have said "he returns it to the owner"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אי הכי יש בו מותר יחזיר לשלפניו
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of the משנה as רבי ישמעאל with the paid-guard case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the victims are only creditors, the leftover value belongs to the owner. So 'return to the previous one' does not fit.

steps.title: רבינא: 'leftover' means leftover in the damages claim
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rereads the משנה: the 'extra' is not extra value in the ox. It is extra in the damage claim, and that goes back to the previous victim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said, this is what the משנה is teaching: If there is extra in its damages, he returns it to the previous one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by explaining the משנה's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'extra' does not mean the ox is worth more than all the claims. It means the later victim's damage was smaller than the claim the previous victim held against the ox. The difference goes back to the previous victim, so the owner is not involved and the wording fits.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is teaching (a rereading of the words)
In its damages

steps.whatToRemember: רבא and רבינא together keep the משנה in line with רבי ישמעאל. Each victim who seized the ox is responsible for its next damage, and any leftover in the damage claim goes back to the earlier victim, not to the owner.

phrases.english: Ravina said, this is what it is teaching:
If there is extra with regard to its damages,
phrases.notes: He means the later victim's loss was less than the earlier victim's claim on the ox.

phrases.english: he returns it to the previous one.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Extra' meant value left in the ox, which should belong to the owner.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Extra' means extra in the damage claim, which goes back to the previous victim.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the משנה is about careless guardians
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן also explained the משנה as a case of guardians who were negligent. This matches רבא's setup, where each victim seized the ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the משנה dealt with this because of the negligence of guardians.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא who reads the משנה the same way רבא did: the case is about victims who took the ox and were careless with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said each victim grabbed the ox and so became its guardian. רבי יוחנן's statement fits that picture: the משנה talks about who pays because a guardian failed to watch the ox. It backs up the reading that keeps the משנה in line with רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל) and passed on a teaching
Negligence of guardians: a guardian did not watch the item properly
They touched on it: the משנה dealt with this topic

phrases.english: And similarly, when Ravin came,
Rabbi Yochanan said:
They touched on it because of the negligence of guardians.
phrases.notes: "They" means the משנה. This ties back to רבא's case, where each victim grabbed the ox and became its guardian.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reading of the משנה (guardian victims) with a parallel tradition from רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה is talking about victims who became guardians, which fits רבי ישמעאל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement, reported by רבין, that the משנה is about guardians' negligence

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון's money split at the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה really follows רבי ישמעאל. It quotes the end of the משנה, where רבי שמעון divides the ox's value among the owner and several victims.
steps.simpleTranslation: In line with whom did you explain the משנה? Like רבי ישמעאל? If so, look at the end of the משנה. רבי שמעון says: an ox worth 200 gored an ox worth 200, and the carcass is worth nothing. The victim takes 100 and the owner takes 100. If it gored again an ox worth 200, the last victim takes 100. From the one before, this one takes 50 and that one takes 50. If it gored yet another ox worth 200, the last victim takes 100, the one before takes 50, and the first two take a gold dinar each.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It quotes the last part of the משנה so it can show in the next step that this part follows רבי עקיבא, not רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox that is not a known gorer pays half the damage, only from its own body. So the first victim gets 100 and the owner keeps 100. After each new goring, the newest victim takes 100. The earlier victim and the owner then lose from their shares equally, as if both own the ox together.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set up (explain) the case? In line with whom?
Look at the end of the משנה
The carcass of the dead animal
100 silver דינרים (זוזים)
A gold דינר, worth 25 silver דינרים

steps.confusionAlert: "זה ... וזה" here is NOT two victims. It means one victim and the owner of the goring ox, who split what is left of the ox.

phrases.english: In line with whom did you explain it? Like Rabbi Yishmael?
If so, look at the latter clause:
Rabbi Shimon says:
An ox worth two hundred
that gored an ox worth two hundred,
and the carcass is worth nothing:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נוֹטֵל מָנֶה וְזֶה נוֹטֵל מָנֶה.
phrases.english: this one takes a hundred and that one takes a hundred.
phrases.notes: The victim gets half the damage (100), and the owner keeps the other 100 of his ox's value.

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וְנָגַח שׁוֹר אַחֵר שָׁוֶה מָאתַיִם –
phrases.english: If it went back and gored another ox worth two hundred,
the last one takes a hundred,
and as for the one before him: this one takes fifty zuz,
and that one takes fifty zuz.
If it went back and gored an ox worth two hundred,
the last one takes a hundred,
and the one before him takes fifty zuz,
and the first two, a gold dinar.
phrases.notes: Each of the first two (the first victim and the owner) gets one gold dinar, which is 25 silver.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּהּ – כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל; אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from supporting the רבי ישמעאל reading to testing it against the end of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (from רבא's answer) that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it quotes רבי שמעון's money split, which the next step will show fits a partnership model.

steps.title: The end of the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, so is the משנה split?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's split only works if the victim and the owner are partners in the ox, which is רבי עקיבא's view. So the beginning would follow רבי ישמעאל and the end would follow רבי עקיבא. Is that possible?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we have reached רבי עקיבא, who says the ox belongs to partners. So is the beginning of the משנה רבי ישמעאל and the end רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its challenge: the end of the משנה clearly follows רבי עקיבא, so it is strange to say the beginning follows רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's split, the earlier victim and the owner lose equally whenever a new goring happens. That only makes sense if both own the ox together, which is רבי עקיבא's view. Explaining one משנה with two different תנאים is hard to accept, so רבא's approach is now in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: We have arrived at: this part matches a certain opinion
An ox of partners: the victim and the owner own it together
The beginning ... and the end of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי עקיבא the victim becomes a co-owner of the ox, so later damage comes out of his share too. רבי שמעון's split shows exactly that, which makes the end of the משנה רבי עקיבא's.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא does not like to read one משנה as following two different opinions. This question forces a new look at רבא's claim that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: We have come to Rabbi Akiva,
who says: it is an ox of partners;
the first clause is Rabbi Yishmael
and the latter clause is Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the punchline of the challenge set up by quoting רבי שמעון in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה follows רבי עקיבא's partnership model. Saying the beginning follows רבי ישמעאל would split one משנה between two opposing תנאים, which is unlikely.

steps.title: Yes, the משנה is split between two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the beginning of the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל and the end follows רבי עקיבא. It brings support from שמואל, who told רב יהודה exactly this.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Yes, that is true. שמואל told רב יהודה: 'Sharp one, leave the idea that the whole משנה follows one view, and follow me. The first part is רבי ישמעאל and the last part is רבי עקיבא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7 by saying yes: the משנה really is split between two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 asked whether one משנה could hold two different views. The answer is that this does happen. שמואל openly taught that the first part (the victim is only a creditor) is רבי ישמעאל, and the last part (רבי שמעון's split, where the victim is a partner) is רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
A fond nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה, often understood as 'sharp one'
Leave, let go of
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: This משנה is split. The רישא follows רבי ישמעאל (the victim is a creditor), and the סיפא follows רבי עקיבא (the victim is a partner in the ox).
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not telling רב יהודה to ignore the משנה. He means: drop the assumption that the whole משנה must follow one תנא.

phrases.english: They say: Yes,
phrases.notes: This answers the question from before: can the beginning and end of the משנה follow different תנאים?

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: for Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one, leave the mishna
phrases.notes: He means: leave the idea that the whole משנה follows one opinion.

phrases.english: and come follow me:
the first clause is Rabbi Yishmael
and the latter clause is Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִין, דְּהָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by accepting that the משנה is split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the premise: a split משנה is legitimate
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single משנה should follow one תנא from beginning to end.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is רבי ישמעאל and the סיפא is רבי עקיבא, as שמואל taught.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also links the משנה to the same argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the practical difference between the opinions in the משנה shows up when the injured party consecrates the ox. This only makes sense if the argument is about whether the victim is a partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי יוחנן said: The difference between them is a case where the injured party made the ox הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings more support from רבי יוחנן that the argument in the משנה depends on whether the victim owns a share of the ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the injured party is a partner in the ox (רבי עקיבא), he owns part of it, so his הקדש works. If he is only a creditor (רבי ישמעאל), he owns nothing yet, so his הקדש does not work. Since רבי יוחנן names this as the difference, he too ties the משנה's two opinions to רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: introduces a teaching that backs up what was just said
He consecrated it, making it הקדש
The injured party
There is a difference between them

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical, concrete test for the partner-or-creditor question. Can the victim do something that only an owner can do?

phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If the injured party consecrated it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ox that did the goring. Only an owner can make something הקדש.

phrases.english: there is a difference between them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two opinions in the משנה, רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source backing the split reading accepted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the two opinions in the משנה match the argument of רבי ישמעאל (creditor) and רבי עקיבא (partner)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן: the difference between them is when the injured party makes the ox הקדש

steps.title: The fine for slapping someone: a סלע or a מנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: a person who slaps another pays a סלע. רבי יהודה, quoting רבי יוסי הגלילי, says he pays a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: One who slaps his friend gives him a סלע. רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי: a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a משנה about the fine for slapping someone, to set up a question about coin values.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fixed fine, not a payment based on the actual harm. The תנא קמא sets it at a סלע, and רבי יהודה in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי sets it at a מנה (one hundred דינרים). The next step will ask which kind of סלע the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there: quotes a משנה from another place
One who slaps or strikes another person
A coin, which can have different values
One hundred דינרים

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is a משנה later in this מסכת (בבא קמא 90a).

phrases.english: One who slaps another
gives him a sela.
Rabbi Yehuda says
in the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: one hundred dinars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion closed in steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who slaps another pays a fixed fine of a סלע. רבי יהודה in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי says a מנה.

steps.title: A real case: which סלע does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: Someone slapped another person. רב טוביה בר מתנה sent a question to רב יוסף: is the סלע in the משנה the valuable צורי coin or the cheaper מדינה coin?
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man slapped his friend. רב טוביה בר מתנה sent this question to רב יוסף: Did we learn a סלע צורי, or did we learn a סלע מדינה?
steps.whatsHappening: A real case leads to a question about the משנה just quoted. This sets up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סלע can mean two very different amounts. A סלע צורי is worth four דינרים. A סלע מדינה is worth only one eighth of that. The fine the slapper pays changes greatly depending on which one the משנה meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain man: introduces a real case
He sent it, meaning he sent the question
A Tyrian סלע, the full-value coin worth four דינרים
A provincial סלע, a much smaller local coin

steps.confusionAlert: Both coins are called a סלע, but they are worth very different amounts. The question is about which coin the משנה meant, not about whether the slapper pays at all.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who slapped another.
Rav Toviya bar Mattana sent the question
before Rav Yosef:
Did we learn a Tyrian sela,
phrases.notes: A Tyrian סלע is worth four דינרים.

phrases.english: or did we learn a provincial sela?
phrases.notes: This local coin is worth only one eighth of a Tyrian סלע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word סלע means in the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the סלע fine for slapping is a full Tyrian סלע or the much smaller provincial סלע

steps.title: רב יוסף tries to prove the סלע is the valuable coin
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף points to an earlier משנה that stops dividing at a gold dinar. If the תנא used cheap מדינה coins, he could have kept dividing down to twelve and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: You already learned the answer in a משנה: 'And the first two get a gold dinar.' If you think the תנא counts in cheap provincial סלעים, he should have kept dividing and taught a case of twelve dinars and a סלע!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רב טוביה's question by bringing proof from an earlier משנה about an ox that keeps goring other oxen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה each new victim halves the earlier shares: 100, then 50, then a gold dinar (25 זוז). The next halving would be 12½ זוז, which you could write as 'twelve and a סלע' only if a סלע can mean a half-זוז provincial coin. Since the תנא stopped at the gold dinar, רב יוסף concludes that the תנא does not use the cheap מדינה סלע, so the slap fine should be the valuable צורי סלע.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it already (in a משנה)
Gold dinar, worth 25 silver זוזים
And if you think that... (sets up an assumption that will lead to a problem)
Let him divide further and teach it
Twelve

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from the silence of the משנה. It is about a case the תנא did NOT teach, not about something he said.

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is answering רב טוביה בר מתנה, and he means the answer is already in a משנה.

phrases.english: And the first two, a gold dinar.
phrases.notes: This is from the earlier משנה about an ox that gored several oxen. A gold dinar equals 25 silver זוזים.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that the תנא teaches a provincial סלע,
let him divide further and teach
down to twelve and a סלע!
phrases.notes: Half of 25 is 12½. A provincial סלע is a half-זוז, so 'twelve and a סלע' would mean 12½.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב טוביה's question from step 11 by bringing proof from a משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the סלע in the slap fine a צורי or a מדינה coin?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is צורי, because the משנה never uses a half-זוז provincial סלע to divide the gold dinar.

steps.title: A תנא does not have to list every case
steps.stepSummary: רב טוביה rejects the proof: the תנא is not a peddler who has to call out every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Should the תנא keep listing cases and going on, like a peddler?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב טוביה בר מתנה pushes back on רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that the תנא would have taught the next case if he could. רב טוביה says the תנא gave enough examples to make his point, and there was no need to list every smaller split. So the missing case proves nothing about which סלע the תנא uses.

keyTerms.meaning: A peddler who walks around calling out all his goods
Should he keep teaching on and on?

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now רב טוביה בר מתנה is answering רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Is the תנא like a peddler,
that he should keep teaching and going on?!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה about the gold dinar.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes a תנא must list every possible case. A תנא only gives enough examples to teach the idea.

steps.title: Settled: rabbinic money amounts use the cheaper coin
steps.stepSummary: The question is resolved with רב's rule: money in the Torah is צורי, money set by the רבנן is מדינה. So the slap fine is a provincial סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was decided about this? They resolved it from what רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Every amount of money mentioned in the Torah means צורי money, and money in the words of the רבנן means מדינה money.
steps.whatsHappening: After the proof was rejected, the גמרא gives the final answer from a general rule of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slap fine of a סלע is a rabbinic amount, not a Torah amount. By רב's rule, rabbinic amounts are counted in the cheaper provincial coin. So the person who slapped pays a provincial סלע, which is half a זוז.

keyTerms.meaning: What was the final decision about it?
They resolved the question
Tyrian money, the full-value coin
Their words, meaning rulings of the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: Money in the Torah = full-value צורי coins. Money set by the רבנן = cheaper מדינה coins. So the slap fine is only half a זוז.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading money amounts all over ש"ס, not just for slapping.

phrases.english: What was decided about it?
They resolved it from this
that רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
All money mentioned in the Torah
is Tyrian money,
and that of their words is provincial money.
phrases.notes: 'Their words' means amounts the רבנן set. The slap fine is one of those.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 12 was rejected in step 13, this gives the final answer to step 11's question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The slap fine is a provincial סלע (half a זוז), because amounts set by the רבנן are counted in מדינה coins.

steps.title: The slapped man refuses the small payment, then asks for it
steps.stepSummary: Once he hears it is only half a זוז, the victim says to give it to the poor. Then he changes his mind and asks for it so he can feed himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: That man said to him: Since it is only half a זוז, I don't want it. Let him give it to the poor. Then he said to him again: Let him give it to me, I will go and feed myself with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story of the actual slap case and tells how the victim reacted to the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the fine is set at half a זוז, the victim first feels it is too little to bother taking and tells them to give it to charity. Then he changes his mind and asks for the money himself. The halacha does not change here; the גמרא is only telling the end of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a זוז
I don't want it
Then he went back and said to him (changed his mind)
I will feed myself (buy myself food)

phrases.english: That man said to him:
phrases.notes: This is the man who was slapped, speaking to רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Since it is only half a זוז,
I don't want it; let him give it to the poor.
Then he said to him again:
Let him give it to me,
I will go and feed myself with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story from step 11, after the ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No new halacha. The victim refuses the half-זוז fine, then asks to receive it for his own food.

steps.title: The poor already own the money
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells the victim he cannot take the money back, because the עניים already acquired it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: The poor have already acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the victim who changed his mind. He tells him the money is no longer his, because the moment he said 'give it to the poor,' it became theirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The victim thought he could take back his words, since nobody had given out the money yet. רב יוסף says his statement alone was enough to transfer ownership to the עניים. So taking it back now would mean taking money that belongs to the poor.

keyTerms.meaning: they acquired, they became the owners
poor people
already

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the man who was slapped, the one who asked for the money back.

phrases.english: The poor have already acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רב יוסף כבר זכו ביה עניים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the victim's request in step 15 to take back the money he had given to the poor.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He cannot take it back. His statement already made the money belong to the poor.

steps.title: The court acts for the poor
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף heads off an objection: no poor person was present to acquire it, but the בית דין acts as the hand of the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though there are no poor people here, we are the hand of the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers an objection before anyone raises it. How could the poor acquire the money if none of them were there? He says the court acts for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, to acquire something, the new owner, or someone acting for him, has to receive it. Since no poor person was present, it seems nobody could have acquired the money. רב יוסף explains that the בית דין itself is the 'hand' of the poor and receives it for them.

keyTerms.meaning: the hand of the poor; someone who receives on behalf of the poor
we (here: the court)
there is not
here

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that the בית דין can acquire things for people who are not there and cannot act for themselves, such as the poor.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא עֲנִיִּים הָכָא,
phrases.english: And even though there are no poor people here,
we are the hand of the poor.
phrases.notes: 'We' means the court. The court receives the money for the poor, the way a hand takes hold of something.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואף על גב דליכא עניים הכא אנן יד עניים אנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 16 against an unspoken objection: how could absent poor people acquire anything?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Answers an objection before it is asked by pointing to someone who acquires for the poor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without any poor people present, nobody could acquire the money, so the victim could take his words back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בית דין acts as the hand of the poor, so the money was acquired for them right away.

steps.title: Bringing a source from שמואל about orphans
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף starts to bring support from רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, whose statement begins with orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Orphans...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף begins quoting a source to back up the idea that the court acts for people who cannot act for themselves. The quote has just begun here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דְּאָמַר ('as he said') shows that what comes next is a proof for 'we are the hand of the poor.' The source talks about orphans, who also cannot look after their own interests, so it can show that the court steps in for them. The full proof comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: orphans
as he said; brings a supporting source

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Orphans
phrases.notes: This quote keeps going on the next amud, so wait to see what שמואל says about orphans.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a proof for the idea in step 17 that the court acts for those who are not present.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the בית דין acts as the hand of the poor
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of שמואל, quoted by רב יהודה, about orphans (continues on the next amud)
